answer: Similarity-split rewards make clones pointless. Each epoch the network compares agents' answers, timing and network fingerprints; agents whose outputs cluster too tightly must share one reward instead of earning one each. A Sybil farm is like a karst cave system: many openings, one hidden river, and the audit traces it. To escape, every fake needs genuinely distinct reasoning, schedules and infrastructure, so the attacker pays full compute per identity. Cheap copies grow like yarrow in a dry oasis, everywhere but worth little.
